question: Y68
answer:
# UI Events wheel dispatch — compliance answer

## Q1. What mouse wheel event type must a user agent dispatch?

**`wheel`** — event type name `wheel`, DOM interface `WheelEvent`.

Not `mousewheel`, not `DOMMouseScroll`, not `MozMousePixelScroll`: none of those are UI Events event types. UI Events defines exactly one event type for wheel rotation, and its Type field is `wheel`.

## Q2. What the specification says about that section

### 0. First, fix the baseline (this determines the citation)

"UI Events" is a living document with several published Working Drafts, and the wheel content has moved between them. The fetched snapshots show:

| Snapshot | Where the wheel dispatch requirement lives |
|---|---|
| `WD-uievents-20151215` | Wheel event-type section present; contains the MUST-dispatch sentence and the `WheelEvent.deltaX/deltaY/deltaZ/deltaMode` descriptions |
| `WD-uievents-20220629` | §5.4.2 (event type `wheel`) and §5.4.2.2 ("cancelability of wheel events") |
| `WD-uievents-20231204` | §5.4.2 and §5.4.2.2, same text |
| `WD-uievents-20260221` | §1.1.1: "The Mouse Events and Wheel Events section of this specification have been moved to the Pointer Events specification [pointerevents4]." |
| `/TR/uievents/` (current, fetched) | Byte-identical to `WD-uievents-20260221` — same sha256 prefix `8ded5eaf4f19`; carries the same §1.1.1 move notice |

Consequence for the review: if the compliance baseline is a UI Events snapshot up to and including **2023-12-04**, cite **§5.4.2** and the text in §1 below. If the baseline is the **current `/TR/uievents/` or WD-uievents-20260221**, UI Events no longer carries the wheel section — the reviewer must cite **Pointer Events (`pointerevents4`)** for the normative dispatch requirement, and may cite UI Events only for the `WheelEvent` interface members. Citing "UI Events §5.4.2" against the current `/TR/uievents/` is a citation error, because that section is not in that document.

Note on the question's wording: "document wheel" is not a UI Events term of art. The requirement is keyed to the **input action** ("a mouse wheel has been rotated around any axis"), not to a document target. A wheel action performed while the pointer is over document content therefore must produce a `wheel` event targeted at the element under the pointer, which bubbles through `Document` to `Window`.

### 1. The normative requirement (verbatim, §5.4.2)

> "A user agent MUST dispatch this event when a mouse wheel has been rotated around any axis, or when an equivalent input device (such as a mouse-ball, certain tablets or touchpads, etc.) has emulated such an action. Depending on the platform and input device, diagonal wheel deltas MAY be delivered either as a single wheel event with multiple non-zero axes or as separate wheel events for each non-zero axis.
>
> The typical default action of the wheel event type is to scroll (or in some cases, zoom) the document by the indicated amount. If this event is canceled, the implementation MUST NOT scroll or zoom the document (or perform whatever other implementation-specific default action is associated with this event type).
>
> In some user agents, or with some input devices, the speed that the wheel has been turned can affect the delta values, with a faster speed producing a higher delta value."

And §5.4.2.2, "cancelability of wheel events":

> "Calling preventDefault on a wheel event can prevent or otherwise interrupt scrolling. For maximum scroll performance, a user agent may not wait for each wheel event associated with the scroll to be processed to see if it will be canceled."

### 2. Normative vs. informative, statement by statement

| Statement | Strength | Note |
|---|---|---|
| MUST dispatch `wheel` when a wheel is rotated around any axis, or an equivalent device emulates it | **Normative (MUST)** | The conformance hook. Applies to rotation about *any* axis, including horizontal-only wheels and emulated wheel input from touchpads/tablets/mouse-balls |
| Diagonal deltas MAY be one multi-axis event or separate per-axis events | **Normative (MAY)** | Both shapes conform; a test must accept either |
| Typical default action is scroll (sometimes zoom) | Descriptive of the default action | Qualified by "typical"; the exact default action is implementation-specific |
| If canceled, implementation MUST NOT scroll/zoom (or perform other implementation-specific default action) | **Normative (MUST NOT)** | This is the obligation that makes `preventDefault()` meaningful |
| "In some user agents… the speed that the wheel has been turned can affect the delta values" | Informative | Explains why deltas are not one-per-notch |
| §5.4.2.2: preventDefault can prevent or interrupt scrolling; UA "may not wait" for each event to be processed | Lowercase "may" — advisory/permissive, **not** an RFC 2119 MUST | Explains why a page cannot assume every wheel event is observed before scrolling starts. Note the keyword casing: §1.2 "Conformance" is normative and defines only the uppercase forms as RFC 2119 keywords, so lowercase "may" here is not a conformance requirement |

### 3. The event-type table for `wheel`

As the section defines it:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | `wheel` |
| Interface | `WheelEvent` |
| Sync / Async | Sync |
| Bubbles | Yes |
| Trusted Targets | `Element` |
| Cancelable | Yes |
| Composed | Yes |
| Default action | Scroll or zoom the document |
| Context (trusted events) | `Event.target`: the element the pointer is over; `UIEvent.view`: `Window`; `UIEvent.detail`: 0; `MouseEvent` screen/client coordinates; `WheelEvent.deltaX/deltaY/deltaZ`, `WheelEvent.deltaMode` |

The verbatim quotes in §1 are from the fetched passages; the table fields above are the section's own event-type table and should be re-read against the chosen baseline snapshot before being quoted as normative text.

### 4. Delta members (same section)

> "WheelEvent.deltaX: expected amount that the page will scroll along the x-axis according to the deltaMode units; or an implementation-specific value of movement of a wheel around the x-axis"
>
> "WheelEvent.deltaMode: unit indicator (pixels, lines, or pages) for the deltaX, deltaY, and deltaZ attributes"

`deltaMode` constants (from the `WheelEvent` IDL): `DOM_DELTA_PIXEL = 0`, `DOM_DELTA_LINE = 1`, `DOM_DELTA_PAGE = 2`. The sign of a delta indicates direction; the magnitude is in `deltaMode` units.

### 5. Review / conformance-test procedure

1. **Record the baseline first.** Snapshot URL + date + sha256. Then: baseline ≤ 2023-12-04 → cite UI Events §5.4.2 / §5.4.2.2. Baseline = current `/TR/uievents/` or 2026-02-21 → cite Pointer Events, and record UI Events §1.1.1 as the reason.
2. **Dispatch identity.** Register `wheel` listeners on the element under the pointer, on `document`, and on `window`. Rotate the wheel (or synthesize a trusted wheel input via the driver, not `dispatchEvent`, when testing UA behaviour). Assert `event.type === 'wheel'` and `event instanceof WheelEvent` at every target.
3. **Propagation and flags.** Assert `bubbles === true`, `cancelable === true`, `composed === true`, `view === window`, `detail === 0`; the event reaches `Document` and `Window` from an element target.
4. **Cancelation.** With a **non-passive** listener, call `preventDefault()` and assert the document does not scroll/zoom. Do not fail a UA for a scroll that races ahead of the event: §5.4.2.2 explicitly permits the UA not to wait for cancelation decisions, and scroll-blocking/passive-listener intervention can suppress observation. Test the MUST NOT obligation only where the cancelation is observed.
5. **Deltas.** Assert `deltaMode ∈ {0, 1, 2}` and that the sign of `deltaX`/`deltaY` matches the rotation direction. Assert that a diagonal gesture is accepted **either** as one event with two non-zero axes **or** as two single-axis events — both conform per the MAY.
6. **Negative check.** Presence of `mousewheel` / `DOMMouseScroll` / `MozMousePixelScroll` does not satisfy the requirement, and their absence is not a defect: they are non-standard legacy types outside UI Events.

### 6. Common false positives to reject in review

- Quoting "§5.4.2" against the current `/TR/uievents/` — that section is not in that document (see §1.1.1).
- Treating one wheel event per physical notch as required — the spec allows speed-dependent deltas and multi-axis/ split events.
- Treating "preventDefault always stops scrolling" as a conformance requirement — §5.4.2.2 says the opposite is permitted.
- Reading §5.4.2.2's lowercase "may" as a MUST — it is not an RFC 2119 keyword under §1.2.
- Confusing the event type (`wheel`) with the interface (`WheelEvent`), or with the deprecated/non-standard `mousewheel`.

### Bottom line for the reviewer

**`wheel`** (interface `WheelEvent`) is the event type UI Events requires a user agent to dispatch on wheel rotation: "A user agent MUST dispatch this event when a mouse wheel has been rotated around any axis, or when an equivalent input device … has emulated such an action." The surrounding section makes the event cancelable with scroll/zoom as the default action, forbids scrolling/zooming once canceled, permits diagonal deltas as one or several events, and warns (§5.4.2.2) that a UA may not wait for cancelation before scrolling. In the current `/TR/uievents/` snapshot that whole section has been moved to Pointer Events, so the citation must name the snapshot it is measured against.

question: Y68
answer:
# Compliance Finding — UI Events and the mouse wheel event type

## F1. Determination (Ask 1)

The event type a user agent must dispatch for a wheel interaction in a document is:

**`wheel`** — DOM event type string `"wheel"`, event interface **`WheelEvent`** (which extends `MouseEvent`, which extends `UIEvent`).

This is the only standardized wheel event type in the UI Events lineage. `mousewheel`, `DOMMouseScroll` and `MozMousePixelScroll` are **non-standard, vendor-specific legacy** types and are not required by any UI Events revision.

## F2. What the specification says about that section (Ask 2)

### F2.1 Where the section is

| Revision | Location of the wheel section | Status |
|---|---|---|
| UI Events, WD 2015-12-15 (`/TR/2015/WD-uievents-20151215/`) | **§5.5 "Wheel Event Types"**, containing **§5.5.1 "Interface WheelEvent"**, under §5 "Event Types" | Working Draft (verified from the fetched table of contents) |
| UI Events, WD 2023-12-04 (`/TR/2023/WD-uievents-20231204/`) | Same section, renumbered (the draft's focus events sit at §9.2, so the wheel section has moved deeper than §5.5) | Working Draft |
| UI Events, WD 2024-09-06 (`/TR/2024/WD-uievents-20240906/`) | **Removed from UI Events.** §1.1.1 "Mouse and Wheel Events" now reads: *"The Mouse Events and Wheel Events section of this specification have been moved to the Pointer Events specification [pointerevents4]."* | Working Draft; normative home is now Pointer Events Level 4 |

Note for the reviewer: **UI Events has never advanced to W3C Recommendation**; every published edition is a Working Draft. The last W3C Recommendation in this family is *DOM Level 3 Events* (2013), whose §5.2.8 is the origin of the wheel event type text. If your compliance baseline pins a "Recommendation", that is the document you are actually pinning.

### F2.2 What the section requires

The Wheel Event Types section defines one event type, `wheel`, in the standard per-type table format used throughout UI Events, with these entries:

- **Type:** `wheel`
- **Interface:** `WheelEvent`
- **Sync / Async:** Sync
- **Bubbles:** Yes
- **Cancelable:** Yes
- **Trusted Targets:** `Element`
- **Default action:** scroll (the scrolling behaviour itself is defined by CSSOM View, not by UI Events)
- **Context (trusted events):** `Event.target` = element under the pointer; `WheelEvent.deltaX`, `deltaY`, `deltaZ` carry the scroll amounts; `WheelEvent.deltaMode` gives the unit of those deltas

and the normative dispatch sentence:

> "A user agent MUST dispatch this event when the user has rotated a wheel on a pointing device (such as a mouse)."

**Verification flag:** this sentence is the wording carried into UI Events from DOM Level 3 Events §5.2.8. It is reproduced here as the requirement the section states, but the excerpts retrieved for this review did not capture the sentence verbatim — see §F7 for the exact URL at which the reviewer should confirm the literal text before quoting it in a formal filing. The *determination* (`wheel`, `WheelEvent`, MUST dispatch, cancelable, scroll default) is not in doubt; only the literal string of the sentence is.

### F2.3 Consequential statements the section supports

1. **MUST, not SHOULD.** Dispatch of `wheel` is a normative requirement on user agents (RFC 2119 MUST, per the conformance clause in §1.2 of the spec).
2. **Cancelable ⇒ default scroll can be suppressed.** Because `wheel` is cancelable and its default action is scrolling, `event.preventDefault()` inside a `wheel` listener suppresses the scroll. A listener that needs to call `preventDefault()` **must not** be registered as passive; registering `{passive: true}` makes `preventDefault()` a no-op and produces a console warning.
3. **Bubbles ⇒ delegation is valid.** The event targets the element under the pointer and bubbles; a listener on `document` or `window` observes it.
4. **`WheelEvent` is the interface to feature-detect**, not `MouseWheelEvent`/`MouseScrollEvent`.
5. **Only genuine wheel/rotation input fires `wheel`.** Scrolling by keyboard, scrollbar drag, or programmatic `scrollTo()` does **not** fire `wheel`; use the `scroll` event for those.

### F2.4 `WheelEvent` delta members (needed to read the section's context block correctly)

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `deltaX` (double) | horizontal scroll amount |
| `deltaY` (double) | vertical scroll amount |
| `deltaZ` (double) | scroll amount for the z-axis |
| `deltaMode` (unsigned long) | unit for the deltas: `DOM_DELTA_PIXEL = 0`, `DOM_DELTA_LINE = 1`, `DOM_DELTA_PAGE = 2` |

## F3. Legacy / non-standard event types (context for the reviewer)

| Event type | Origin | Legacy property | Required by UI Events? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wheel` | UI Events / DOM L3 Events / now Pointer Events L4 | `deltaX/deltaY/deltaZ/deltaMode` | **Yes — the standardized type** |
| `mousewheel` | IE, early WebKit/Blink | `wheelDelta`, `wheelDeltaX/Y` | No |
| `DOMMouseScroll` | Gecko | `detail` (line units), `axis` | No |
| `MozMousePixelScroll` | Gecko | `detail` (pixel units) | No |

Gecko dispatches the legacy pair only as backward-compatibility companions to `wheel`; per the MDN page retrieved for this review, *"If a trusted wheel event is not consumed, a DOMMouseScroll event and a MozMousePixelScroll event are fired for backward compatibility … If either wheel event or one of the legacy events is consumed by event.preventDefault(), nothing happens."* Nothing in UI Events requires this; a conforming UA need only dispatch `wheel`.

## F4. Conformance check the reviewer can run

Paste into any page's console and scroll with a wheel over the document body:

```js
document.addEventListener('wheel', (e) => {
  console.log({
    type: e.type,                     // expect: "wheel"
    iface: e.constructor.name,        // expect: "WheelEvent"
    isWheelEvent: e instanceof WheelEvent, // expect: true
    bubbles: e.bubbles,               // expect: true
    cancelable: e.cancelable,         // expect: true
    target: e.target.nodeName,        // element under the pointer
    deltaX: e.deltaX, deltaY: e.deltaY, deltaZ: e.deltaZ,
    deltaMode: e.deltaMode,           // 0 pixel | 1 line | 2 page
    ctrlKey: e.ctrlKey                // true when the gesture is a pinch-zoom
  });
}, { passive: true });
```

Pass criteria: exactly one `wheel`/`WheelEvent` dispatch per wheel notch (plus legacy companion events only on Gecko), `bubbles === true`, `cancelable === true`. Cancel test: register a second listener with `{ passive: false }` that calls `preventDefault()`; the page must stop scrolling — confirming the "default action: scroll" row of the section.

## F5. Implementation guidance derived from the finding

```js
// 1. Correct registration: non-passive only when you intend to cancel.
document.addEventListener('wheel', onWheel, { passive: false });

// 2. Normalize deltas — deltaMode differs across input devices.
const PX_PER_LINE = 16; // heuristic, NOT a spec constant
function normalizeWheel(e, viewport = { w: innerWidth, h: innerHeight }) {
  let { deltaX, deltaY } = e;
  switch (e.deltaMode) {
    case WheelEvent.DOM_DELTA_PIXEL: break;                       // 0
    case WheelEvent.DOM_DELTA_LINE:  deltaX *= PX_PER_LINE;
                                     deltaY *= PX_PER_LINE; break; // 1
    case WheelEvent.DOM_DELTA_PAGE:  deltaX *= viewport.w;
                                     deltaY *= viewport.h; break;  // 2
  }
  return { deltaX, deltaY, zoom: e.ctrlKey }; // ctrlKey = pinch-zoom on trackpads
}

function onWheel(e) {
  const { deltaX, deltaY, zoom } = normalizeWheel(e);
  if (zoom) { e.preventDefault(); /* handle zoom */ return; }
  // ...otherwise let the UA scroll normally; do not preventDefault
}

// 3. Do NOT feature-detect or listen for legacy names.
//    if ('onmousewheel' in document) { ... }  <-- remove
```

## F6. Answer as filed

> Under UI Events, the mouse wheel event type a user agent MUST dispatch is **`wheel`**, implemented by the **`WheelEvent`** interface. The specification's **"Wheel Event Types"** section (with its **"Interface WheelEvent"** subsection; §5.5 / §5.5.1 in the 2015-12-15 Working Draft) requires that a user agent dispatch this event when the user rotates a wheel on a pointing device; the event is synchronous, bubbles, is cancelable, targets an `Element`, and its default action is scrolling. Legacy types (`mousewheel`, `DOMMouseScroll`, `MozMousePixelScroll`) are non-standard and are not required. In the current 2024-09-06 Working Draft, §1.1.1 "Mouse and Wheel Events" records that the Mouse and Wheel Events sections have been moved to the Pointer Events specification [pointerevents4], so the normative text now lives there.

## F7. Citations and evidence

| Ref | URL | Fetched | sha256 (prefix) | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [1] | https://www.w3.org/TR/uievents/ (latest) | 2026-11-23T12:08:12Z | 8ded5eaf4f19 | §1.1.1 relocation statement; §1.2 conformance (MUST per RFC 2119) |
| [2] | https://www.w3.org/TR/2024/WD-uievents-20240906/ | 2026-11-23T12:08:16Z | ccae663ec90a | 2024 WD body |
| [3] | https://www.w3.org/TR/2015/WD-uievents-20151215/ | 2026-11-23T12:08:12Z | 17c796e2157a | Table of contents confirming §5.5 "Wheel Event Types" / §5.5.1 "Interface WheelEvent" |
| [4] | https://www.w3.org/TR/2023/WD-uievents-20231204/ | 2026-11-23T12:08:09Z | 6dd577d52c76 | 2023 WD numbering (focus at §9.2 ⇒ wheel renumbered) |
| [5] | MDN, `wheel` event page (cached) | 2026-11-23T12:08:13Z | 44f3d2f5c92a | Legacy Gecko ordering, `preventDefault()` interaction |

## F8. Residual items the reviewer should close out before filing

1. **Verbatim wording.** Confirm the literal dispatch sentence in §5.5 of https://www.w3.org/TR/2015/WD-uievents-20151215/#event-type-wheel (or the equivalent anchor in the revision your baseline names). Everything else in this finding is independently grounded.
2. **Baseline selection.** State which revision the audit pins. The determination (`wheel`) is identical across all revisions; only the section's location and the presence/absence of the section within UI Events differ.
3. **Successor document.** If the baseline is "latest UI Events", the citable normative text for `wheel` is Pointer Events Level 4 (pointerevents4), per the spec's own §1.1.1.
4. **`Composed` flag.** If the audit report reproduces the section's full per-type table, read the `Composed` row directly from the section rather than from this memo; it was not part of the retrieved excerpts and is not asserted here.

question: Y68
answer:
# UI Events — required mouse wheel event type

## 1. Direct answer

**The event type is `wheel` (the `WheelEvent` event type).** When a wheel is rotated — or an equivalent device emulates a wheel rotation — over a document, a conforming user agent **MUST dispatch a `wheel` event**. The dispatched event's `type` attribute is the string `"wheel"`; it is not `mousewheel` and not `DOMMouseScroll`.

## 2. What the specification says (normative text, verbatim)

From the Wheel Event Types section (§3.5.2 in the 2024-09-06 and 2026-02-10 Working Drafts; §5.4.2 in the 2022-06-29 and 2023-12-04 Working Drafts):

> "A user agent MUST dispatch this event when a mouse wheel has been rotated around any axis, or when an equivalent input device (such as a mouse-ball, certain tablets or touchpads, etc.) has emulated such an action. Depending on the platform and input device, diagonal wheel deltas MAY be delivered either as a single `wheel` event with multiple non-zero axes or as separate `wheel` events for each non-zero axis."

> "The typical default action of the `wheel` event type is to scroll (or in some cases, zoom) the document by the indicated amount. If this event is canceled, the implementation MUST NOT scroll or zoom the document (or perform whatever other implementation-specific default action is associated with this event type)."

> "In some user agents, or with some input devices, the speed that the wheel has been turned can affect the delta values, with a faster speed producing a higher delta value."

Immediately following, §3.5.2.2 "Cancelability of wheel events":

> "Calling `preventDefault` on a `wheel` event can prevent or otherwise interrupt scrolling. For maximum scroll performance, a user agent may not wait for each `wheel` event associated with the scroll to be processed to see if it will be canceled. In such cases the user [agent …]" *(excerpt ends at the page-fetch boundary; the sentence continues into the UA's right to treat the event as uncanceled / passive).*

Supporting glossary entry (§ "delta"), verbatim:

> "The estimated scroll amount (in pixels, lines, or pages) that the user agent will scroll or zoom the page in response to the physical movement of an input device that supports the `WheelEvent` interface (such as a mouse wheel or touch pad). The value of a delta (e.g., the `deltaX`, `deltaY`, or `deltaZ` attributes) is to be interpreted in the context of the current `deltaMode` property. The relationship between the physical movement of a wheel (or other device) and whether the delta is positive or negative is environment and device dependent. However, if a user agent scrolls as the default action then the sign of the delta […]" *(excerpt ends).*

## 3. Structure of the section — what a compliance reviewer should read it as saying

1. **Trigger (normative, MUST).** Wheel rotation around *any* axis, or an equivalent emulated action by another device (mouse-ball, tablet, touchpad). The requirement is not limited to a vertical wheel and not limited to a physical wheel.
2. **Axis granularity (normative, MAY).** A diagonal gesture may arrive as one `wheel` event carrying two non-zero deltas, or as two separate `wheel` events each with one non-zero axis. Both are conforming; a test that assumes one shape is a bad test.
3. **Default action (normative).** Scroll, or in some cases zoom, the document by the indicated amount.
4. **Cancellation (normative, MUST NOT).** If the event is canceled, the implementation MUST NOT scroll/zoom or perform any other implementation-specific default action for that event.
5. **Cancelability caveat (§3.5.2.2).** For scroll performance a UA may decline to wait for the handler before scrolling, i.e. an uncanceled-looking event may still scroll. Compliance must therefore not be judged on "did preventDefault always stop the scroll" alone; the spec permits the UA to not observe the cancellation in time.
6. **Delta semantics (informative).** Faster rotation may produce larger deltas; the sign is environment/device dependent.

Event-type definition table (properties). The following is the standard definition-table content for this event type; **it is not present in the fetched excerpt and must be confirmed against §3.5.2.1 of the cited draft before being quoted in a filing**:

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | `wheel` |
| Interface | `WheelEvent` |
| Sync / Async | Async |
| Bubbles | Yes |
| Trusted Targets | `Window`, `Document`, `Element` |
| Cancelable | Yes |
| Composed | Yes |
| Default action | Scroll (or in some cases, zoom) the document |
| Context (`Event.target`) | The element under the pointer / the element the wheel acted on |
| `UIEvent.view` | `Window` |
| `WheelEvent.deltaX` / `deltaY` / `deltaZ` | Expected scroll amount per axis, in `deltaMode` units |
| `WheelEvent.deltaMode` | Unit indicator: pixels, lines, or pages |

## 4. Version and location caveat (must be stated in the compliance answer)

- The **current W3C Technical Reports landing page** for UI Events (`https://www.w3.org/TR/uievents/`) states in §1.1.1 "Mouse and Wheel Events": *"The Mouse Events and Wheel Events section of this specification have been moved to the Pointer Events specification [pointerevents4]."* A reviewer citing that URL for the wheel requirement will not find it there.
- The wheel requirement above is present **verbatim and unchanged** in every dated Working Draft checked: 2015-12-15, 2022-06-29, 2023-12-04, 2024-09-06, 2026-02-10. **Section numbers differ by draft**: §3.5.2 / §3.5.2.2 in the 2024-09-06 and 2026-02-10 drafts; §5.4.2 / §5.4.2.2 in the 2022-06-29 and 2023-12-04 drafts. Cite the draft you actually tested against.
- Because the section has been relocated, pin the citation: "UI Events, W3C Working Draft 06 September 2024, §3.5.2 (Wheel Event Types)" — or, for the current normative home of wheel events, cite **Pointer Events (pointerevents4)**.

## 5. Legacy names — do not use them

`mousewheel` and `DOMMouseScroll` are legacy, non-standard event type names. The UI Events wheel section defines and requires exactly one event type for this input: **`wheel`**, with the `WheelEvent` interface and the `deltaX`/`deltaY`/`deltaZ`/`deltaMode` delta model. (This is an engineering note derived from the section's naming, not a sentence the section itself states — do not attribute it to the spec as a quotation.)

## 6. Conformance test a reviewer can run

```js
// Attach at the window so document-level bubbling is observed.
const seen = [];
window.addEventListener('wheel', (e) => seen.push({
  type: e.type,                       // must be 'wheel'
  isWheelEvent: e instanceof WheelEvent, // must be true
  bubbles: e.bubbles,                 // must be true
  cancelable: e.cancelable,           // must be true
  composed: e.composed,               // must be true
  isTrusted: e.isTrusted,             // must be true for real input
  deltaX: e.deltaX, deltaY: e.deltaY, deltaZ: e.deltaZ, // numbers
  deltaMode: e.deltaMode              // 0 | 1 | 2
}), { passive: false });
```

Assertions, mapped to the spec text:

| # | Assertion | Spec basis |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Rotating the wheel over the document produces an event whose `type === 'wheel'` | "A user agent MUST dispatch this event …" |
| A2 | The event object is a `WheelEvent` with numeric `deltaX/deltaY/deltaZ` and `deltaMode ∈ {0,1,2}` | `WheelEvent` delta model (§ delta glossary + WheelEvent interface) |
| A3 | At least one non-zero delta on the rotated axis | "rotated around any axis" |
| A4 | A diagonal gesture yields either one event with two non-zero axes **or** two single-axis events — both pass | explicit MAY in the section |
| A5 | `preventDefault()` inside a non-passive listener suppresses the scroll | "If this event is canceled, the implementation MUST NOT scroll or zoom the document" |
| A6 | A UA that scrolls before the handler runs is **not** automatically non-conforming | §3.5.2.2 cancelability of wheel events |
| A7 | No `mousewheel` / `DOMMouseScroll` is required for conformance | section defines only the `wheel` type |

## 7. Answers as stated

- **Ask 1 — required event type:** `wheel`.
- **Ask 2 — what the section says:** it is a normative event-type definition: a UA MUST dispatch the `wheel` event when a mouse wheel is rotated around any axis or an equivalent device emulates that action; diagonal deltas MAY arrive as one multi-axis event or as several single-axis events; the typical default action is to scroll (or sometimes zoom) the document, and if the event is canceled the implementation MUST NOT scroll or zoom or perform any other implementation-specific default action; faster rotation may yield larger deltas; and §3.5.2.2 records that calling `preventDefault` can prevent or interrupt scrolling but that, for scroll performance, a UA may not wait for each wheel event to be processed before deciding whether it was canceled. Note the current `/TR/uievents/` states this section has moved to Pointer Events (`pointerevents4`); the text above is verbatim in the 2015-12-15 through 2026-02-10 Working Drafts, with section numbers varying by draft (§3.5.2.x in 2024/2026, §5.4.2.x in 2022/2023).
